note: Triennial election of Lisnaskea Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961 (no poll was needed). The Impartial Reporter of 18 May 1961, p. 7, reports the nominations: no contest ('the first time for many years that there has not been a contest for one of the Lisnaskea seats'), no nomination for Rosslea, whose outgoing member Mr. Thomas Beagan was nominated for Eshnadarragh, and new members for Cross, Kilmore, Eshnadarragh and Mullynagowan. Other members are those named in the Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (4 and 11 May 1961). Rosslea was left without a member (also Belfast News-Letter, 29 May 1961, p. 5). Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Aghakillymaude, Clonkeelan, Derrysteaton, Drumshemuck and Springtown. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Lisnaskea, Derrylea, Belleisle, Castlebalfour, Armagh Manor, Drummully, Dresternan, Magheraveely and Brookeborough. Samuel Hutchinson, W. Whittendale and a third member were co-opted at the first meeting (Fermanagh Herald, 17 June 1961, p. 6); co-options, not election results. Rosslea's outgoing member, Thomas Beagan, stood for Eshnadarragh, so no retiring member remained to be deemed re-elected for it. Returned unopposed.
